segments: We had a supply teacher in history.
I've got a small story from yesterday.
I went into a meeting room and all the chairs had been moved, so I had to work out where to sit.
What happened in your history lesson?
The teacher didn't know where we were up to.
The date was already on the board.
What did the supply teacher ask you to do?
Read the page about the Industrial Revolution.
Did you manage to do that?
He said answer the questions at the bottom.
I did questions one to six.
Was there anything difficult about the lesson?
How did you feel when he called you that?
What did you do when he called you Vincent?
What happened at the end of the lesson?
I put mine on the front desk.
So the supply teacher didn't know where the class was up to, you read the Industrial Revolution page and answered six questions, and he called you Vincent more than once even after you corrected him.
He collected the books at the end.

Therapist. You're right. Child. I added that. Therapist. What did you do when he called you Vincent? Child. I said it's Victor. He said sorry. Therapist. Did he remember after that? Child. For a bit. Then he did it again. Therapist. What happened at the end of the lesson? Child. He collected the books. I put mine on the front desk. Therapist. Child. He collected the books at the end. Yes. Therapist. Thank you, Victor. That's all for today. Child. Okay.

written.summary: The child told that they had a supply teacher in history. The teacher didn't know where they were up to. The child got their book out. The date was already on the board. Everyone in their class read the page about the Industrial Revolution. The teacher asked them to answer the questions at the bottom. The child did questions one to six. The teacher kept calling them Vincent. The child said it's Victor. The teacher said sorry. The teacher did it again. The child put their book on the front desk. The teacher collected the books at the end.
